title: Electric Motor Temperature
provider: Department of Power Electronics and Electrical Drives (LEA), Paderborn University; released via Kaggle.

keys: Estimating Electric Motor Temperatures With Deep Residual Machine Learning

separation: The related LEA current transition, stationary torque grid, and thermal drive-cycle releases involve distinct acquisitions and lack a common test identifier. Do not join individual files across releases.
rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 per Kaggle release https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ ; attribute the above depositors. This batch distributes independently derived nonoverlapping-window and model summary tables, provided under the same CC BY-SA 4.0. The source CSV, ZIP and article are not mirrored.
query_log: DataCite query: titles.title:(motor AND temperature) AND creators.name:(Kirchg*); returned the version DOI. Followed version DOI to Kaggle, checked release comparison and the cited paper.
Zenodo titles on PMSM experimental/identification and motor test benches also returned simulated fault studies and manuscript-only deposits; these have not been counted as separate measured releases.

paper.title: Estimating Electric Motor Temperatures With Deep Residual Machine Learning
paper.locators: Section III, Tables I and II, pp. 7482–7483: 52 kW torque-controlled traction PMSM and 210 kW speed-controlled load, sampling at 2 Hz, synchronous ADCs, embedded type-K thermocouples and telemetry for mean of four magnet sensors. Paper reports about 140 h and excludes torque from its input features. Kaggle v3 reports the 185 h expanded collection.

method: Output nominal one-minute winding change = winding[j+120]-winding[j], stepping j by 120 only inside each profile. Adjacent windows share one endpoint. Regress on 1, mean((id/100)^2 + (iq/100)^2) and mean(abs(rpm)/1000) during the observed interval. The second model also uses initial coolant-minus-winding and yoke-minus-winding temperature divided by 20. Fit ordinary least squares on 68 profiles, evaluate the remaining complete profile and repeat. Persistence predicts zero change. Pooled RMSE is weighted by held-out window counts. Test-window drive inputs are observed.
limitations: Profile order in the release determines sample order; no separate time column is provided. “60 seconds” assumes the published 2 Hz cadence. Only intervals with a full endpoint are kept.

This is a single motor and fixed split protocol. Model comparisons are conditional descriptions; they do not identify thermal derating or causal cooling rates. The file does not include the commanded torque, pre/post limit values, saturation flags or a separately identified torque transducer. The Kaggle card calls torque an achieved quantity; this batch uses the temperatures as independent measured targets.
reproduce: Python >=3.11 with numpy and pandas. OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python derive_motor_thermal.py SOURCE_V3_ZIP OUT
